turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Niamh, you're all checked. Blood pressure 118 over 76, pulse 94, oxygen 98 percent, temperature 36.6. In you go.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come on in. Claire can stay if you like. What brought you down today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah I'm grand, really. Just a small bit tired, that's the height of it. She made me come.
[SEG0004] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She is not grand. She's wrecked, and she stops halfway up the stairs at home, gasping.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Niamh, this tiredness — when did it start?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): A few months back. It's only mild, I'm well able to—
[SEG0007] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She's not well able. Asleep on the couch every evening after work. And wait till you hear about the periods.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long have the periods been heavy?
[SEG0009] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She won't even ring her own GP. Says she's too busy with work.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): About a year. Roughly since this time last year. They're heavy, yeah, but I'm not bleeding to death.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): On a bad day, how many pads would you go through?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't be counting. A good few, more than I used to. Sometimes there's clots, only little ones, nothing mad.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with the shortness of breath?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the breathlessness — is it only on the stairs, or at rest as well?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Only if I rush the stairs. I'm grand on the flat. It's not a big deal.
[SEG0017] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Tell him about your hair. The brush is full of it every morning and she pretends it's nothing.
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Everyone loses hair, Claire. But yeah, it's coming out more. I couldn't tell you when that started.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any tablets at home? And any drug allergies?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): No allergies, none. I've iron tablets, only I don't take them right.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ferrous sulphate 200 milligrams, by mouth?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, that's the one. GP said once a day, for the tiredness.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): And you're taking it every day, are you?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family history — thyroid trouble, or anaemia, in the family?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Anaemia, I don't think so. Thyroid, em—
[SEG0027] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Mam had an underactive thyroid. On tablets for years.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations? And anything ongoing, diabetes or heart trouble?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): No operations, never. No diabetes, no heart trouble. I'm never sick, so this feels like a fuss.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): God, no. Never have.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Grand, I'll have a quick look. The insides of your lower eyelids are pale. Chest is clear, no crackles.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Heart sounds are normal, no murmur. And there's no swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thinking it through — heavy periods for a year, tiredness, breathless on the stairs, and you're pale. Most likely this is an iron deficiency anaemia from the bleeding.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hair coming out can fit with that. I wouldn't rule out a thyroid problem either, with your mam's history and the fatigue, so we'll check.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll send you for bloods today: a full blood count, a ferritin, and your thyroid function. That'll tell us if the iron is down and whether the thyroid is in on it.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): A pelvic ultrasound we might arrange if the bleeding doesn't settle. I won't book it today.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): If you say so. I'm not mad on scans, but grand.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take the ferrous sulphate every day, not just now and again. If you get proper chest pain, or you're breathless just sitting, come straight in, don't wait. I'll see you back in a fortnight with the results.
[SEG0040] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll get her here. And I'll stand over her with the tablets, since she won't.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah yeah. Are we done? I've work in the morning.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Pallor is supported, but body_site 'general' is not stated; lower eyelids/pale only.
Breathless while sitting is supported; 'there is chest pain' overstates transcript's 'proper chest pain'.
bad.text: Come straight in if there is chest pain or breathlessness while sitting (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Exertional shortness of breath was specifically described by the caregiver as stopping halfway up the stairs at home, gasping; this functional detail is not recorded.
Chest pain was asked about and the patient gave an equivocal positive response ('sometimes, not really'); this is not accurately captured and should not be treated as simply absent.
Family history of anaemia was asked about and denied ('Anaemia, I don't think so').
Past medical history included the patient stating she is 'never sick', indicating no ongoing illnesses apart from the current issue; not recorded except for diabetes/heart trouble specifically.
The doctor advised to seek urgent review only for proper chest pain or if breathless while sitting; the recorded advice broadens this to any chest pain, which is inaccurate.
Pelvic ultrasound was not being booked now; it would only be arranged later if the bleeding does not settle. The 'I won't book it today' part is not explicitly recorded.
